description.en: Name the rooms, rent a bedsitter, talk to the landlord, buy stima tokens and share the chores.
description.so: Magacaw qolalka, kirayso bedsitter, la hadal milkiilaha guriga, iibso tokens-ka korontada oo qaybso shaqada guriga.

body.en: Most people in Nairobi rent. A single room is one room with a shared toilet; a bedsitter has its own small kitchen corner and bathroom; then come one-bedroom and two-bedroom flats. Rooms are often in a plot run by a caretaker. You pay kodi (rent) to the mwenye nyumba (landlord), usually by M-Pesa, plus a deposit when you move in.
body.so: Dadka Nairobi intooda badan way kiraystaan. Single room waa hal qol oo musqushiisu wadaag tahay; bedsitter wuxuu leeyahay jiko yar iyo musqul u gaar ah; kadib waxaa jira guryo hal qol-jiif ama laba qol-jiif leh. Qolalka badanaa waxay ku yaallaan plot uu maamulo caretaker (ilaaliye). Kodi (kirada) waxaad siisaa mwenye nyumba (milkiilaha guriga), badanaa M-Pesa, iyo deposit marka aad soo guurto.

examples.en: I'm looking for a house to rent.

examples.sw: Kodi ni elfu nane kwa mwezi.
examples.en: The rent is eight thousand a month.

body.en: Add -ni to a place noun to say 'in' or 'at': nyumba → nyumbani (at home), jiko → jikoni (in the kitchen), chumba → chumbani (in the room), shamba → shambani (at the farm). Use it with niko / yuko / wako: Niko nyumbani (I'm at home), Yuko jikoni (she's in the kitchen). To count rooms: chumba kimoja, vyumba viwili, vyumba vitatu.
body.so: Ku dar -ni magaca meesha si aad u tiraahdo 'gudaha' ama 'ku': nyumba → nyumbani (guriga), jiko → jikoni (jikada gudaheeda), chumba → chumbani (qolka gudihiisa), shamba → shambani (beerta). La isticmaal niko / yuko / wako: Niko nyumbani (guriga ayaan joogaa), Yuko jikoni (jikada ayay ku jirtaa). Tirinta qolalka: chumba kimoja, vyumba viwili, vyumba vitatu.

examples.en: The children are in the room.

body.en: Kenyans say stima for electricity (Tanzanians say umeme). Most homes buy prepaid tokens with M-Pesa; when they run out, the lights go off. Power cuts happen too: Stima imepotea. Water is sometimes cut off, so many homes keep a tank, and people cook with a gas cylinder (mtungi wa gesi) or a charcoal jiko.
body.so: Kenyaanku korontada waxay ku yiraahdaan stima (Tansaaniyaanku waxay yiraahdaan umeme). Guryaha badankood waxay M-Pesa ku iibsadaan tokens horay loo bixiyo; marka ay dhammaadaan, nalalku way damaan. Koronto go'idduna way dhacdaa: Stima imepotea. Biyaha mararka qaar waa la jaraa, sidaa darteed guryo badan waxay hayaan haan, dadkuna waxay wax ku kariyaan dhalada gaaska (mtungi wa gesi) ama jiko dhuxul ah.

examples.en: The power has gone off again!

body.en: At someone's door or gate, say Hodi! instead of only knocking. The family answers Karibu! When you visit, expect to be offered tea; it is polite to accept at least a little.
body.so: Albaabka ama irridda qof, dheh Hodi! intii aad garaaci lahayd oo keliya. Reerku wuxuu kuugu jawaabayaa Karibu! Marka aad booqato, filo in shaah lagu siiyo; edeb ayay tahay inaad ugu yaraan wax yar ka qaadato.

examples.so: Ma soo galaa? Guriga qof ma joogaa?

title.en: Ushago: the home in the village

body.en: Many town people also have a rural home where their parents or grandparents live. In Sheng it is ushago; in standard Swahili people say nyumbani or shambani. At holiday time, such as Idd or Christmas, buses out of Nairobi fill up with people going ushago.
body.so: Dad badan oo magaalada deggan waxay sidoo kale leeyihiin guri miyiga ah oo ay waalidkood ama awoowayaashood ku nool yihiin. Sheng-ka waa ushago; Sawaaxiliga caadiga ahna dadku waxay yiraahdaan nyumbani ama shambani. Waqtiga fasaxyada, sida Ciidda ama Kirismaska, basaska ka baxaya Nairobi waxaa ka buuxa dad u socda ushago.

examples.so: Bisha soo socota ayaan miyiga u tegi doonnaa.

note.en: Nyumbani = at home. The plural is also nyumba.
note.so: Nyumbani = guriga (gudihiisa). Wadartuna waa nyumba.

note.en: Plural: vyumba. Chumba cha kulala = bedroom.
note.so: Wadarta: vyumba. Chumba cha kulala = qolka jiifka.

note.en: Many Kenyans simply say sitting room.
note.so: Kenyaan badan waxay si fudud u yiraahdaan sitting room.

note.en: Jiko is both the kitchen and a charcoal stove. Jikoni = in the kitchen.
note.so: Jiko waa jikada iyo sidoo kale burjikada dhuxusha. Jikoni = jikada gudaheeda.

note.en: Choo kiko wapi? = Where is the toilet? Kenyans also say washroom.
note.so: Choo kiko wapi? = Musqushu xaggee ku taal? Kenyaanku sidoo kale waxay yiraahdaan washroom.

note.en: Kuoga = to take a bath or a shower.
note.so: Kuoga = qubeysi / maydhasho.

note.en: Funga mlango = close the door. Fungua mlango = open the door.
note.so: Funga mlango = albaabka xir. Fungua mlango = albaabka fur.

note.en: Plural: funguo. In everyday speech many Kenyans say funguo for one key too.
note.so: Wadarta: funguo. Hadalka maalinlaha ah Kenyaan badan funguo ayay u yiraahdaan xitaa hal fure.

note.en: At the door, Kenyans first call Hodi! (may I come in?). The family answers Karibu!
note.so: Albaabka, Kenyaanku marka hore waxay yiraahdaan Hodi! (ma soo galaa?). Reerkuna wuxuu ku jawaabaa Karibu!

note.en: Add -ni to a place to say 'in' or 'at': jiko → jikoni, chumba → chumbani.
note.so: Ku dar -ni meel si aad u tiraahdo 'gudaha' ama 'ku': jiko → jikoni, chumba → chumbani.

note.en: Karibu ndani = welcome, come inside.
note.so: Karibu ndani = soo dhawoow, soo gal.

items.so: bedsitter (qol keliya oo jiko iyo musqul leh)

note.en: A single room is cheaper: one room with a shared toilet. A one-bedroom has a separate bedroom.
note.so: Single room waa ka jaban yahay: hal qol oo musqushu wadaag tahay. One-bedroom wuxuu leeyahay qol jiif oo gooni ah.

note.en: In Kenyan towns a plot is a building or compound full of rooms for rent, often with a caretaker.
note.so: Magaalooyinka Kenya, plot waa dhismo ama xero ay ka buuxaan qolal kiro ah, badanaa leh ilaaliye (caretaker).

note.en: Mpangaji = tenant. Nyumba za kupanga = houses for rent.
note.so: Mpangaji = kiraystaha. Nyumba za kupanga = guryo kiro ah.

note.en: Kodi also means tax. Kodi ya nyumba = house rent.
note.so: Kodi sidoo kale waxay ka dhigan tahay cashuur. Kodi ya nyumba = kirada guriga.

note.en: Usually one month's rent, paid together with the first month.
note.so: Badanaa waa kirada hal bil, waxaana lala bixiyaa bisha ugu horraysa.

note.en: From English 'steam'. Umeme is the textbook word and is also understood in Kenya.
note.so: Waxay ka timid erayga Ingiriisiga 'steam'. Umeme waa erayga buugaagta, Kenya-dana waa la fahmaa.

note.en: Most homes have prepaid meters. You pay by M-Pesa and get a number to type into the meter.
note.so: Guryaha badankoodu waxay leeyihiin mitirro horay loo bixiyo. Waxaad ku bixisaa M-Pesa, waxaadna helaysaa lambar aad ku qorto mitirka.

items.en: The water has been cut off

note.en: Many homes keep a water tank (tanki) for these days.
note.so: Guryo badan waxay hayaan haan biyo (tanki) maalmahaas.

note.en: Kenyans cook with gas cylinders (mtungi wa gesi) and refill them at the shop.
note.so: Kenyaanku waxay wax ku kariyaan dhalooyinka gaaska (mtungi wa gesi), dukaankana ayay ka buuxiyaan.

note.en: Zima taa = switch off the light. Washa and zima also work for the TV and the radio.
note.so: Zima taa = nalka dami. Washa iyo zima sidoo kale waxaa loo isticmaalaa TV-ga iyo raadiyaha.

note.en: Use kufua for clothes and kuosha for dishes, hands and cars.
note.so: Kufua dharka ayaa loo isticmaalaa, kuosha-na weelasha, gacmaha iyo baabuurta.

note.en: A Kenyan expression from English 'deck'.
note.so: Waa oraah Kenyan ah oo ka timid erayga Ingiriisiga 'deck'.

note.en: Shambani = at the farm, in the countryside.
note.so: Shambani = beerta, miyiga.

note.en: In the village, especially among herders, the boma is the family's compound with its houses and animals.
note.so: Tuulada, gaar ahaan xoolo-dhaqatada, boma waa xerada reerka oo leh guryaheeda iyo xoolaheeda.

note.en: Many rural homes still cook on firewood. Kuokota kuni = to collect firewood.
note.so: Guryo badan oo miyiga ah weli waxay wax ku kariyaan xaabo. Kuokota kuni = xaabo guratid.

note.en: Nairobians go ushago for holidays such as Idd and Christmas, when the city goes quiet.
note.so: Dadka Nairobi waxay u tagaan ushago fasaxyada sida Ciidda iyo Kirismaska, marka magaaladu aamusto.

note.en: Cows, goats, sheep and camels. Kufuga = to keep animals.
note.so: Lo', ari iyo geel. Kufuga = xoolo dhaqasho.

explain.en: 'Where is the toilet?' – 'It's there, near the kitchen.'
explain.so: 'Musqushu xaggee ku taal?' – 'Waa halkaas, jikada agteeda.'

meaning.en: Put the tea on the table.

explain.en: 'Where is the key?' – 'It's on the table.' Mezani = on the table (meza + -ni).
explain.so: 'Furuhu xaggee buu yaal?' – 'Miiska ayuu saaran yahay.' Mezani = miiska dushiisa (meza + -ni).

lines.en: May I come in?
Welcome! Come inside.
Thank you. Is Mama in?

lines.sw: Yuko jikoni. Kaa chini, nikuletee chai?
lines.en: She's in the kitchen. Sit down; shall I bring you tea?
lines.so: Jikada ayay ku jirtaa. Fadhiiso, shaah ma kuu keenaa?

explain.en: Someone is at the door. Answer Karibu! (come in).
explain.so: Qof baa albaabka taagan. Ugu jawaab Karibu! (soo gal).

lines.sw: Habari, mzee. Natafuta nyumba ya kupanga.
lines.en: Hello, sir. I'm looking for a house to rent.
lines.so: Iska warran, adeer. Guri kiro ah ayaan raadinayaa.

lines.sw: Kuna chumba kimoja. Kodi ni elfu nane kwa mwezi.
lines.en: There is one room. The rent is eight thousand a month.
lines.so: Hal qol baa jira. Kiradu waa siddeed kun bishii.

lines.en: And how much is the deposit?

lines.sw: Deposit ni kodi ya mwezi mmoja.
lines.en: The deposit is one month's rent.
Okay. Can I see the room?

explain.en: 'How much is the rent?' – 'It's ten thousand a month.'

prompt.en: I want to rent a house

lines.en: Why is it dark? Has the power gone off?
lines.so: Maxaa mugdi u ah? Korontadii ma go'day?

lines.en: No, the tokens have run out.
Then buy tokens on your phone.
Okay, I'm buying them right now.
lines.so: Hagaag, hadda isla markiiba waan iibsanayaa.

options.en: There is a power cut in the area

explain.en: 'The gas has run out!' – 'Oh no! I'll buy another one.'
explain.so: 'Gaaskii wuu dhammaaday!' – 'Ka xumahay! Mid kale ayaan iibsanayaa.'

meaning.en: The water has been cut off today.

lines.en: Zawadi, have you swept?

lines.sw: Ndiyo, mama. Nimefagia na nimepiga deki.
lines.en: Yes, Mum. I've swept and mopped the floor.
lines.so: Haa, hooyo. Waan xaaqay, sagxaddana waan masaxay.

lines.sw: Asante. Sasa osha vyombo, mimi ninapika.
lines.en: Thank you. Now wash the dishes; I'm cooking.
lines.so: Mahadsanid. Hadda weelasha dhaq, anigu wax baan karinayaa.

extra.heard: Leo ni zamu yako kuosha vyombo.

explain.en: 'Today it's your turn to wash the dishes.' – 'Okay, I'll wash them right now.'
explain.so: 'Maanta waa kaalintaada inaad weelasha dhaqdo.' – 'Hagaag, hadda ayaan dhaqayaa.'

meaning.en: Baraka is sweeping the living room.

lines.en: How was upcountry?
Very good. I helped Grandpa on the farm.
lines.so: Aad buu u fiicnaa. Awoowe ayaan beerta kaga caawiyey.

lines.en: And the animals?

lines.sw: Iko salama. Babu ana ng'ombe kumi.
lines.en: They're fine. Grandpa has ten cows.
lines.so: Way nabad qabaan. Awoowe wuxuu leeyahay toban lo'.

question.en: Where did Otieno help his grandfather?
question.so: Xaggee buu Otieno awoowihiis ka caawiyey?

explain.en: 'When will you go upcountry?' – 'Next week, by bus.'
explain.so: 'Goorma ayaad miyiga u tegaysaa?' – 'Toddobaadka soo socda, bas ayaan raacayaa.'

meaning.en: My grandmother cooks with firewood at the farm.
meaning.so: Ayeeyaday beerta xaabo ayay wax ku karisaa.
